guide.summary: Santo Domingo's museum, Zapotec archaeological sites, textile and craft workshops, with breakfasts, dinners, cafés and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
highlights: Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca (Santo Domingo)
Museo de Sitio de Monte Albán
guide.tip: INAH lists the Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca as open Tuesday to Saturday only and Zaachila as open Thursday to Sunday only, so save a Monday for Monte Albán's site museum, Mitla, Yagul or Atzompa, which list daily hours.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: INAH lists the Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca as open Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00 to 16:00, and Zaachila as open Thursday to Sunday, 10:00 to 16:00. Monte Albán's site museum, Mitla, Yagul and Atzompa list daily hours.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: INAH lists $210 MXN for foreign visitors at the Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca, Mitla, Yagul and Monte Albán's site museum, whose entry is included in the archaeological zone ticket. Atzompa is free, and Zaachila lists $145 MXN for foreign visitors.

toolkit.label: Booking
toolkit.copy: Casa Oaxaca El Restaurante and Origen take reservations through OpenTable, while Selva asks groups of six or more to arrange ahead by WhatsApp. INAH recommends booking a Monte Albán guided tour two days in advance.

toolkit.label: Site rules
toolkit.copy: INAH's pages for Mitla, Yagul, Atzompa and the Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca bar smoking, food and pets, and the museum also bans flash. Professional cameras carry an extra fee at the Museo de las Culturas and Monte Albán's site museum.

guide.dek: Plan museum and ruin days around INAH's listed opening days, then book Centro dinners ahead.
intro: Start in Centro, where the Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca fills the former Convent of Santo Domingo de Guzmán on Macedonio Alcalá. INAH's page lists it as open Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00 to 16:00, with foreign visitors paying $210 MXN, and you can't bring food, pets or a flash. On Hidalgo, the Museo Textil de Oaxaca lists current exhibitions including 'Ladbeej – El textil teñido con cochinilla', plus textile workshops through November 2026, among them an autumn dyeing workshop from 24 to 26 November. On the same street, the Centro Cultural San Pablo occupies what its operator calls Oaxaca's first Dominican convent.

Monte Albán's site museum, on the Ignacio Bernal road above the city, lists daily hours of 08:00 to 16:30 with last entry at 16:00, and its admission is included in the archaeological zone ticket; INAH recommends booking a guided tour two days ahead. East along Highway 190, Mitla lists 08:00 to 17:00 daily with last access at 16:30, and Yagul lists 08:00 to 17:00 with last entry at 16:00. Atzompa is free and lists daily hours of 08:00 to 16:00, while Zaachila opens Thursday to Sunday only, 10:00 to 16:00. Mitla, Yagul and Atzompa bar smoking, food and pets.

For meals, Zandunga on García Vigil publishes daily hours, serving breakfast from 9 AM to 12 PM and lunch and dinner from 12 PM to 11 PM. Casa Oaxaca El Restaurante on Constitución opens at 13:00, closing at 23:00 Monday to Saturday and 21:00 on Sunday, and takes bookings through OpenTable, as does Origen on Avenida Juárez. Pitiona on Allende handles reservations by email and WhatsApp. In Jalatlaco, Terraza Centro at City Centro by Marriott serves from 7:00 to 22:00 daily, and in Centro, Cocina Azul at Hotel Azul opens 7:30 to 22:30 with a Sunday buffet breakfast.

For drinks, Campante Bar sits on Hotel Azul's terrace and opens Monday to Saturday 15:00 to 23:00 and Sunday 11:00 to 20:00, and Pabilo Café in the same hotel serves coffee, Oaxacan chocolate and house-baked bread. Selva on Macedonio Alcalá seats you at shared, lounge-style tables and asks groups of six or more to arrange ahead by WhatsApp. With children, the Museo Infantil de Oaxaca occupies the restored former railway station on Calzada Madero, and the BS children's library in Xochimilco is free for children and teenagers. For a craft-village day, the Jacobo y María Ángeles workshop in San Martín Tilcajete says it opens 365 days a year.
summaryCards: Pair the Museo de las Culturas de Oaxaca in the former Santo Domingo convent, open Tuesday to Saturday per INAH, with Monte Albán's site museum, which lists daily hours.
Start with breakfast at Cocina Azul or Zandunga, then browse the exhibitions at the Museo Textil de Oaxaca on Hidalgo.
Reserve Casa Oaxaca El Restaurante or Origen through OpenTable, and remember that Zaachila opens Thursday to Sunday only.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several hours come from pages that are undated (INAH Lugares pages, Origen, Pitiona) or carry older footers (Fundación Alfredo Harp Helú venue pages © 2022, Chocolate Mayordomo © 2021, Jacobo y María Ángeles with 2025 items), so treat them as published rather than current. INAH's Museo de las Culturas page lists Tuesday to Saturday hours yet also mentions free Sunday entry for Mexican citizens. Pitiona's Spanish and English hours differ for Saturday, and MUFI's own site gives Constitución 201 while its operator lists Reforma 504. Hours were not published for the Museo Textil de Oaxaca, El Asador Vasco, Quinta Real Oaxaca's venues, Pabilo Café or Selva. The Monte Albán zone page returned 404, so Monte Albán rests on the INAH site museum page. Sites that could not be read: Mezcaloteca, Café Brújula and Mezcal Real Minero (HTTP 429), El Destilado and Cafebre (403), In Situ Mezcalería (expired certificate), Sabina Sabe (TLS error), Expendio Tradición (connection closed), Rey Campero (522), Boulenc and Pan:AM (no working site), and the Oaxaca state culture site (500). Bakery coverage is thin: only Pabilo Café, which mentions house-baked bread, was confirmed.
